claim: A case worth storing carries problem description, solution and outcome (including failures), plus an explanation of why; Kolodner, Aamodt-Plaza and the LLM triples/tuples (state,action,reward; P,S,O,M; Q,S,E,A) all share this core.
agent_test: Write S9 records with the three fields plus a one-line why; ablate dropping outcome or why at equal tokens.

claim: Failures should be stored and indexed, but only help when the memory format can use them: strategy-level items gain from failures (ReasoningBank Shopping 46.5 to 49.7), success-only trajectory/workflow memories gain little or lose (AWM 44.4 to 42.2).
agent_test: Run two S9 stores (success-only vs success+failure with a distilled lesson) on a fixed ARC/BrainTeaser slice.

claim: Distilled, abstract strategy items (title, description, short content) beat raw trajectories or concrete exemplars in agent memory: ReasoningBank WebArena 48.8 vs Synapse 42.1, AWM 44.1, no memory 40.5; AWM beats Synapse by +5.0 element accuracy; Dynamic Cheatsheet curated beats full history.
agent_test: Compare raw-trajectory S9 entries vs distilled lessons at equal retrieved tokens.

claim: Abstraction is not always better: ExpeL ALFWorld retrieval-only 55% beat insights-only 50%, while HotpotQA insights-only 36% beat retrieval-only 31%; DS-Agent found paired (task, working script) cases beat free-text human insights.
agent_test: Store both a lesson and one concrete worked example per case; ablate each by task type.

claim: Retrieving more cases does not help: Memento K=1 gets most of the gain (59.9 to 63.6 F1), peak at K=4 (64.5), flat to K=32; ReasoningBank best at 1 item (49.7 vs 44.4 at 4); DS-Agent performance falls as cases rise.
agent_test: Cap retrieved cases at 1, 2, 4 at equal prompt tokens and measure.

claim: Case memory gain is real but shrinks with repeated passes: Memento w/o CBR rises 78.65 to 84.47 over five passes vs parametric CBR 80.46 to 85.44 (gap about 1.8 down to 1.0); CBR gain on DeepResearcher +6.7 F1 / +8.2 PM.
agent_test: Measure memory gain vs number of passes on our agent; check whether retries alone erase it.

claim: Agents copy retrieved cases (experience-following): output similarity tracks input similarity (r near 1 at high input similarity), so wrong or low-quality stored cases propagate errors.
agent_test: Plant a wrong-outcome case similar to a test item; measure how often the agent copies it.

claim: Admission control matters: adding every run gave worse results than a small fixed memory when the filter is weak (RegAgent add-all 55.48 vs fixed 67.53); a strict filter reached 70.95. Kolodner and Aha IB3 give the same admission/noise-filter rule.
agent_test: Only write S9 entries that passed an external check; compare against write-everything at equal tokens.

claim: Deleting records tied to poor later results helps only with a reliable evaluator; periodic deletion cuts memory size with small loss; noisy evaluators make history-based deletion unreliable.
agent_test: Track a Laplace-smoothed success/retrieval count per record and evict low-utility ones; compare with no eviction.

claim: How accurate outcome labels must be is contested: ReasoningBank judge was 72.7% accurate and success stayed 47.6 to 52.4 for judge accuracy 100 to 50 percent, while Xiong found coarse automatic evaluators give flat or declining curves.
agent_test: Vary outcome-label noise injected into S9 and measure the slope.

claim: Index on abstract features of the failure or structure, not surface problem text: TextBFGS error-keyed retrieval 74.36 vs problem-keyed 58.12 on cross-domain MBPP Plus (problem-keyed slightly better in-domain); CBR-to-SQL masked skeletons beat plain RAG; Kolodner's anticipatory indexing says the same.
agent_test: Key S9 on error type/operator rather than task wording; test cross-domain. Small benchmarks, preliminary.

claim: Multi-part case retrieval helps modestly: CBR-RAG hybrid similarity over question, support, entities with the full case in the prompt scored 0.9141 vs 0.8967 no retrieval (+1.94%), significant one-tailed p<0.05, 32 test cases.
agent_test: Low priority; effect small and on a tiny test set.

claim: Memory format effect in document QA: no single format wins; a mixed memory (chunks, triples, facts, summaries) is best on average (HotpotQA 82.11 F1 iterative), but this was documents, not agent experiences.
agent_test: Try one lesson plus one raw example as a mixed record; low confidence transfer.

claim: Models trained on examples generalise by case matching, not rule following: leave-square-out accuracy collapses inside the held-out region (100% on random split); rule-following fine-tuning repairs it.
agent_test: Not directly testable in a prompted agent; a reason surface-similar cases may mislead.

claim: In classic instance-based learning, storing only misclassified cases (IB2) saves memory (7.5% to 71% stored) but is noise-sensitive (26.3% of stored instances noisy at 10% attribute noise); success-tracking IB3 fixes it with accuracy near or above IB1 on most of six sets.
agent_test: Record utility counts per case as in IB3; compare to store-only-failures.

claim: Self-generated successful trajectories alone lift performance and curation adds more: gpt-4o-mini ALFWorld 0.73 to 0.89 (0.91 with database curation), SQL 0.75 to 0.79, Wordcraft 0.55 to 0.64; database growth beat upgrading the model on ALFWorld.
agent_test: Seed S9 from the agent's own verified solves and track the growth curve.

claim: Repeated trials improve memory quality: ReasoningBank MaTTS parallel k=1 49.7 to k=5 55.1 (no memory 39.0 to 42.2); Agent KB shows removing its Refine/adapt step gives the largest drop.
agent_test: Run k attempts, distill the contrast into an S9 item; compare to best-of-k without memory.

claim: Short verbal lessons after failure raise results (Reflexion ALFWorld 130/134; HotpotQA self-reflection +8% over episodic-only), supporting a lesson field in the outcome part.
agent_test: Ablate the lesson field.

claim: Memory gains depend on model strength: Dynamic Cheatsheet helps Haiku AIME 2024 10.0 to 36.7 but AIME 2025 only to 13.3; Sonnet Game of 24 only 12 to 14; GPT-4o full-history fell 20.0 to 13.3.
agent_test: Test S9 at more than one model size.

claim: Useful bank size is small for LLM agents (Memento saturates near 3k items) even though classic CBR case bases grew from thousands to millions; the effect of bank size beyond this is unmeasured.
agent_test: Plot gain vs bank size on our agent; likely small banks suffice.

claim: No study found tests case field ablations (drop outcome vs explanation vs context) directly in LLM agents; most compare whole memory designs, so which field earns its tokens is unknown.
agent_test: Run field-level ablations (problem/solution/outcome/why/context) at equal tokens.

claim: Storing the concrete case and a distilled lesson together beat either alone on repeated-template tasks: Memp GPT-4o ALFWorld test 42.14 none, 56.43 script, 74.29 trajectory, 77.86 both; Qwen2.5-72B 41.25, 61.88, 69.57, 77.19. Not on every score (Claude on TravelPlanner).
agent_test: Store each S9 record as problem + solution + outcome + a one-line lesson; compare against lesson-only and case-only at equal tokens.

claim: A cheap retrieval key (task wording) gets most of the benefit of a smarter key. Random memories alone gave much of the gain on TravelPlanner (GPT-4o 71.93 none, 74.59 random, 73.38 query key, 76.02 keyword key). Retrieving too many items eventually hurts.
agent_test: Use task wording plus an error-type tag; cap retrieved cases at about 3 to 5.

claim: Outcome label noise: strategy-style memory tolerated label flipping (ReasoningBank 47.6 to 50.6 across 100 to 50 percent judge accuracy vs 39.0 none; ACE tolerated harmful updates up to one in five, but every-step corruption gave 66.7 vs 70.7 base), while raw-trajectory demos with coarse judges did worse than a frozen bank (Xiong). Tolerance depends on format and on merge and dedupe.
agent_test: Inject 10, 20 and 50 percent flipped outcomes on one slice with 3 seeds; compare lesson-style and raw-case records.

claim: Memory and extra sampling look complementary, not substitutes. CER Forum: sampling alone 43.1, memory alone 37.7, both 52.6. ReasoningBank best-of-N without memory 39.0 to 42.2 while parallel scaling with memory reached 55.1. No equal-token comparison exists.
agent_test: Run equal-token arms: no memory with N tries, memory with 1 try, memory with N tries.

claim: Memory gain depends on task similarity: Evo-Memory ReMem gain vs within-dataset similarity r = 0.717 (Gemini-2.5-flash) and 0.563 (Claude-3.7); AIME-25 and GPQA show small gains. Training-Free GRPO still gained 2.7 and 5.4 points on AIME24/25 for a 671B model from 100 training samples.
agent_test: Expect small gains on ARC or brainteasers unless cases share structure; measure gain vs task similarity on our slice.

claim: Benefit does not grow with model size: ReasoningBank gains +8.3 (flash), +7.2 (pro), +4.6 (Claude-3.7); Evo-Memory says smaller models benefit most; Training-Free GRPO helped Qwen3-32B and Qwen2.5-72B but a 32B reasoning model (QwQ) fell 27.5 to 25.5. Memory from a strong model helps a weaker one (Memp, Qwen2.5-14B, +5 percent completion).
agent_test: Test one weak and one strong backbone with identical records; also strong-written records read by the weak model.

claim: Misleading cases are followed by GPT-4-class models: MINJA injection above 95 percent, attack success above 70 percent in half the configurations; AgentPoison about 80 percent attack success with poison below 0.1 percent. Measured mitigations: more benign neighbours, strict admission, utility-based deletion, merge and dedupe.
agent_test: Record provenance and verification status per case; refuse unverified near-duplicates as demonstrations.

claim: Retrieved workflows must be adapted, not replayed: Agent KB raw workflow 58.18 vs refined 61.21 vs no refine 55.15 (GAIA pass@1, GPT-4.1); Memp found revising memory after failure beat plain append.
agent_test: Add an adapt step between retrieving a case and using it.

claim: Content-type ablation exists, field ablation does not: CER Forum 37.7 full, 33.3 without skills, 35.1 without page dynamics; Agent KB removes pipeline stages, not fields. Problem, solution, outcome, explanation and context at equal tokens remain untested.
agent_test: Run the field ablation ourselves.

claim: Bank size and eviction over long horizons stay thin: Agent KB shows 100 examples already useful and 500 better on code; Xiong's capped banks (100 and 180) beat a frozen bank with utility eviction; nothing tests beyond about 4k items or beyond 5 passes with eviction counts.
agent_test: Plot gain vs size at 50, 200 and 1000 cases with and without utility eviction.
